records.title: Aeromedical Aspects of Aircrew Training
records.locator: Title, Contents and national chapters, RTO-MP-21
records.evidence_note: This public 90-page DTIC scan contains the national chapters available at printing. Chapters 7 (Turkey) and 8 (Poland) are identified in the contents as unavailable at printing. The chapter locators preserve printed and PDF pages.

records.title: Aviation Medicine Training of Royal Air Force Aircrew
records.locator: RTO-MP-21, chapter 1, print pp. 1-1 to 1-3, DCS and denominator on p. 1-2 (PDF p. 11)
records.evidence_note: The 1997 chamber series occurred in North Luffenham, before the training centre moved to RAF Henlow in January 1998. Morris gives 1,559 students exposed in 279 runs and explicitly reports no DCS cases that year. Repeat attendance, staff-year exposure totals and systematically ascertained delayed cases are unreported. The narrative presents a separate instructor loss-of-consciousness event and discusses possible trainee reluctance to report mild symptoms. Morris says that data for 1990–1996 were unavailable.

observations.group: Students exposed to altitude during training, as reported
observations.note: Chamber subset of 2,152 course students. Exposure attendance is explicit. A repeat-attendance rule and delayed surveillance window are unavailable.

records.title: Aerospace Physiology Training for German Federal Armed Forces
records.evidence_note: Valentiner reports approximately 5,300 exposures since 1995 with three rule-out diagnoses. The suspected cases resolved on ground-level oxygen. Final diagnoses, role-specific case and exposure counts and the exact date of follow-up are unspecified. The chapter describes training profiles both with and without an inside observer, so staffing cannot be converted into an exposure total.

observations.note: The source gives an approximate denominator and provisional diagnoses. Confirmation and post-exposure surveillance are unknown.

records.title: Aviation Physiology and Medicine Training in the Royal Netherlands Air Force & Aeromedical Institute
records.locator: RTO-MP-21, chapter 16, sections 1.2.3 and 1.8 (PDF pp. 70 and 74)
records.evidence_note: The 1998 statistics give 699 under hypobaric training and no known DCS cases. The general text also reports no DCS cases over the preceding two years without an exposure denominator for that wider period. The chapter is for the 1998 workshop, so retain the author’s year label without assuming 31 December closure. The programme includes international military and civilian visits. The subtotals sum to 1,182, exceeding the 1,106 all-training count. The categories can overlap or reflect an inconsistency. The source gives no repeat-attendance rule, staff-specific numerator or denominator, or standardized delayed surveillance.

observations.group: Aircrew counted in hypobaric training for the author’s 1998 reporting period
observations.note: The zero is for known cases. The 699 is the 1998 hypobaric trainee tally, with follow-up and repeat attendance unspecified.
